title: Churn Investigation Lab Notebook
content:
OVERVIEW
Purpose: A lightweight, reproducible investigation template framed as a lab notebook for rapid churn diagnostics. Use this when an account cancels or a renewal soft-fails and we need a clear timeline, hypotheses, and counterfactuals for QBRs and internal learning.

Scope: Focused on single-account post-cancellation analysis (90–180 day window). Includes: signal collection checklist, timeline reconstruction, hypothesis mapping, counterfactual actions with estimated impact, and a renewal-tracker snapshot format suitable for QBR inclusion.

QUICK START (first 90 minutes)
1) Create this doc in the account folder and tag stakeholders.
2) Triage signals: billing, product usage, support, legal/compliance, CSM notes. Pull last 90 days for each.
3) Schedule 30–45 minute internal sync with CSM, AM, product owner, and SRE/infra if outages suspected.
4) Draft timeline and 3 top hypotheses — publish to the account’s investigation folder.

DATA & SIGNALS CHECKLIST (pull these immediately)
- Billing: invoice history, disputes, PO changes, payment failures, discount schedule.
- Usage: API calls per endpoint, median/95th latency, error rate, token/embedding volumes, model variants used.
- SLA incidents: SRE incidents for the account (last 6 months).
- Support tickets: threads, time-to-first-response, resolution cycles, sentiment in messages.
- CSM notes: meeting notes, promises/commitments, escalations.
- Contract/closure: renewal notice dates, termination clause triggers, legal threads.
- Competitive intel: mentions of competitors in notes or procurement communications.

RAW TIMELINE (reconstruct by timestamp; keep raw observations)
- 2025-08-04 09:12 — CSM weekly check-in: customer raised rising latency; agreed to follow up with infra. (source: CSM notes)
- 2025-08-07 14:20 — Support ticket #8942 opened: "intermittent 5xx errors on /v1/generate". Ticket reopened twice. (source: ticketing system)
- 2025-08-09 11:03 — Billing: invoice dispute submitted for July usage spike; customer asked for throttling review. (source: finance)
- 2025-08-12 16:40 — On-call incident (INC-1021): brief spike in error rate; mitigated by autoscale, but customer saw degraded latencies. (source: SRE runbook)
- 2025-09-01 10:00 — Procurement sends RFP shortlist to 3 vendors; Redwood mentioned as option. (source: procurement email chain)
- 2025-10-02 00:00 — Non-renewal notice received. Reason: "cost and inconsistent performance". (source: legal)

OBSERVATIONS (what jumps out)
- Multiple short outages co-occurred with months of elevated token usage — bill shock + performance degradation.
- CSM notes show promises to follow up but limited technical evidence attached to customer comms.
- Procurement/competitive activity began after the first billing dispute.

HYPOTHESIS MAPPING (ranked)
1) Cost shock + value mismatch (High confidence): Unexpected usage pattern increased spend; customer perceived value per dollar dropped.
2) Performance regressions driving buyer fear (Medium-high): Latency spikes during peak windows eroded user confidence.
3) Sales/Procurement timing (Medium): Procurement engaged competitors during dispute period and used downtime as leverage.
4) Feature gap / model quality (Low-medium): Specific model outputs didn’t meet evolving accuracy needs.

EVIDENCE & DATA TO VALIDATE EACH HYPOTHESIS
- Cost shock: invoice diffs, per-route token spike, changes in batching/sequence lengths.
- Performance: p95 latency pre/post incidents, request error rates per model version, SLO compliance windows.
- Procurement: email threads indicating procurement timelines, competitor mentions, RFP dates.
- Model quality: eval score changes, customer report examples showing regression.

COUNTERFACTUAL PLAYBOOK (what could have meaningfully changed the outcome)
Format: [Action] — [Owner] — [Earliest deploy] — [Estimated impact] — [Notes]
- Proactive spend alerting & guided throttles — CSM + Billing — within 7 days — Medium-high — If customer had received automated "unexpected spend" alert with recommended throttles, they might not have escalated to dispute.
- Fast lane incident remediation (CSM-triggered SRE runbook) — SRE/CSM — 24–48 hours — High — A dedicated, visible incident bridge and status updates to the customer could have prevented erosion of trust.
- Temporary credit + usage review session — Finance + CSM — 3–5 days — Medium — Partial credit paired with a technical review shows ownership and reduces churn risk.
- Short-term model pinning to known-good variant — Product + CSM — 2–3 days — Medium — If model quality was a factor, a rollback/pinning could reduce user-facing regressions.

RENEWAL-TRACKER SNAPSHOT (paste into QBR / include in renewal pipeline)
Columns: Account | Renewal Date | Status | Root Cause (top 1) | Counterfactual Action | Estimated ARR at Risk | Next Steps Owner
Example row: "AcmeCo | 2025-10-01 | Lost | Cost shock + perf | Spend alert + credit + SRE bridge | $180k | CSM: Maya Chen"

QBR INPUT (2–4 bullets for the customer-facing QBR or internal exec brief)
- Summary: Account non-renewed due to compounded cost shock and intermittent latency spikes during July–August 2025; procurement engaged competitors during dispute window.
- Key learnings: need for automated spend alerts and fast-lane incident bridges for strategic accounts.
- Action plan (90 days): implement spend alert beta for top 50 accounts; build CSM-triggered SRE bridge template; pilot temporary credit policy for disputed invoices.

MEETING AGENDA TEMPLATE (loss retro, 60 minutes)
1) Facts & timeline (10 min): read raw timeline aloud.
2) Evidence review (15 min): product & billing owners present data pulls.
3) Hypotheses and counterfactuals (15 min): prioritize top 2 changes we could have made.
4) Action commitments (15 min): owners, deadlines, measurement.
5) Quick wins & follow-ups (5 min): blockers and next meeting.

NOTES TO LOG (keep raw quotes and snippets):
- Insert verbatim customer emails that reference "cost" or "performance" — do not paraphrase until validated.
- Link support ticket excerpts and timestamps — preserve thread structure.

METRICS TO TRACK (post-mortem effectiveness)
- % of strategic accounts with automated spend alerts (goal: 80% within 90 days).
- Mean time to incident-bridge creation for CSM-triggered events (goal: < 2 hours).
- % of disputes resolved with partial credit + technical review (goal: increase by 30%).

NEXT ACTIONS (owner / ETA)
- Pull final invoice and token usage CSV for 2025-07 to 2025-09 — Finance (Liam) / 2026-01-20.
- SRE to extract p95/p99 latency for account-specific routes and incidents — SRE (Jordan) / 2026-01-18.
- Draft spend alert email verbiage and throttle options — CSM (Maya) / 2026-01-25.
- Schedule loss retro with AM, product PM, SRE, billing — Maya / 2026-01-22.

VERSION NOTE (lab notebook style):
- 0.1 2025-11-05 initial scaffold and checklist (Maya).
- 0.2 2025-11-12 added raw timeline and support ticket excerpts (Liam).
- 0.3 2026-01-15 updated hypotheses after SRE latency extract (Jordan).

APPENDIX (paste raw outputs here)
- Placeholder: support ticket text, SRE incident log excerpts, invoice diff CSV snapshot.

END OF LAB NOTE.

Use this doc as the canonical, time-stamped single source for any exec QBR or product retro related to this account. Keep raw evidence unedited and record each change as a new version line in the header.
